analysis:
The only change in this PR is documentation: a new "Prompt preparation and admission" section in docs/reference/configuration.md (head lines ~498-507). It documents DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE, _MB, _VERIFY, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_TEMPLATE_LOOPS and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_COLD_LOAD_RELEASE. The supplied units are base-side excerpts (lines 312-597), and the patch excerpt is truncated at the last row. No source code, no implementation of PromptTokenCache.swift or ChatTemplateLoopRewrites.swift, and no config-default changes were provided, so I cannot verify the documented behavior.

Security-relevant notes for later passes:
1. The documented token-piece cache holds token IDs derived from plaintext prompts (A-001) in provider RAM, per tokenizer. It is described as scoped to the request's prefix-cache scope, which the coordinator derives per account and model build (see T-041). If that scoping is implemented as described, it adds no new cross-account channel. It could add a same-account TTFT timing signal that extends SEC-035/T-041. Whether it is truly keyed by cacheSalt and not shared across accounts is unverified, and T-041 does not yet mention this tier.
2. The cache is on by default and is turned off by the global DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE disable. That interaction should be checked in code.
3. The VERIFY background re-tokenization mismatch fallback and the TEMPLATE_LOOPS rewrites change how templates render before tokenization. A divergence would affect prompt fidelity, not confidentiality, and only if the load-time comparison is wrong.
4. The statement "Forwarded by LaunchAgent" is unverified against LaunchAgent.inferencePassthroughEnvKeys.

No concrete regression is established from the documentation alone. The companion code change needs review for scope keying, memory residency and release of the prompt-piece storage, and for whether T-041/T-028 should be updated.
